name: BZ wave fragments (sub-excitable)
description: Light-sensitive Belousov–Zhabotinsky (Oregonator). Under strong light (phi ≈ 0.084) the medium is sub-excitable: a broken wave neither spreads into a full wave nor dies at once, but travels as a compact fragment. Top: a lone fragment. Below: two fragments meet head-on, overlapping by half — colliding excitation waves annihilate, so the overlap cancels and the leftover halves carry on as shorter fragments (the basic gate of Adamatzky's collision-based computing). Fragment length is an unstable balance point (as theory says for a uniform medium): at this phi they slowly widen, and a little more light makes them shrink instead — stabilising them is next on the list. Things to try: paint phi high (≈0.1) for light barriers fragments die at, or lower (≈0.07) for channels where they widen; lower phi globally (≈0.05) for full excitable waves and spirals; the seed brush excites.
